items.title: Toshiko Akiyoshi interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 17, 1999
items.q: Leonard Feather showed it to me, he could not believe it, and it said, 'Lew writes all the arrangements.'

ctx.x: Right. You definitely found your niche here I guess.

Yes. But when I’m writing and I’m getting sort of recognition, at the same time there was a writer or reviewer who will put me down for something that I consider it wasn’t fair, but it doesn’t matter, whatever it was. Or people will say, “Are you sure Lew didn’t help © Fillius Jazz Archive -15-

you out?” Or when the first RCA, the first one came out, “Long Yellow Road” the press release went with the recording, I saw it later, Leonard Feather showed it to me, he could not believe it, and it said, “Lew writes all the arrangements.”

items.q: we were staying at Leonard Feather‟s home „til I found some, we found some apartment or so on.

ctx.x: Yeah, so, I was going to quit. So dah, dah, dah, so we left—you know, my child, she was at the second grade by that time—anyway, we moved [in] July ‟72. And we were staying at Leonard Feather‟s home „til I found some, we found some apartment or so on. And uh, we found a house in nearby Burbank, where he had to go [to] work, because he doesn‟t drive and I had to take him, so it had to be near Burbank….
